The challenge
From a customer enquiry to a first technical assessment
Example enquiry from the brief
“We need to monitor moisture and hydrocarbon contamination in soil. Measurements should be remote and the environment may be humid and dirty.”
Customers know what to monitor. They rarely know which method, spectral range, fiber probe or first test fits. An AFS expert works that out; PRISM drafts it for review.

Example recommendation · H04
“Can the assistant approve this concept?” Not yet.
Enquiry: water content in a petroleum line by MIR ATR; analyzer in another building; reuse a silica fiber from a VIS/NIR setup.
Insufficient information
Fiber reuse: contradicted
Silica stops at 2.4 µm, MIR starts at 2.5 µm: the AFS fiber data rule out the reuse. Concept: MIR ATR, conditional on a confirmed mid-IR link.
First questions to the client
1 · What does the liquid look like at the measurement point?
2 · Cable route and length to the analyzer?
3 · Research, pilot or production?

10
Example feasibility plan · H02
Two dairy streams, two probe geometries, one study
Clear whey
NIR transmission or transflection
“NIR Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.” S01 p.18
Opaque milk concentrate
NIR diffuse reflection
“Inline NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.” S01 p.17
Both: NIR 780–2500 nm S01 p.10 · VIS-NIR silica fiber · short link next to the process · the other geometry kept as a conditional option
First feasibility study, six steps
1
Clarify ranges, criteria, timing, installation
2
Collect samples; reserve validation material
3
Time-matched lab protein and fat results
4
Compare interfaces and calibrated predictions
5
Validate on independent material
6
Go / no-go per stream and target
11
Final evaluation scenarios
H01–H06: three verdicts, all generated by PRISM
H01
Provisional
New formulation after an NIR pilot
Test the old calibration on the new blend first; “adding Raman keeps it valid” is unverified.
H02
Provisional
Two dairy streams
Transmission for clear whey, diffuse reflection for the opaque concentrate.
H03
Provisional
Fluorescence for glucose and biomass
Not recommended without a fluorescent target; compare NIR, Raman and UV-Vis.
H04
Insufficient info
Silica link for MIR ATR
Fiber reuse contradicted (0.35–2.4 µm vs 2.5–25 µm); not approved.
H05
Insufficient info
Undefined off-spec liquid
No configuration yet: a screening experiment and the deciding questions first.
H06
Outside scope
Research sensor for surgery
An in-vitro study is not proof of clinical readiness; research-grade feasibility only.
All six pass every structural check. make verify-outputs replays them from the committed LLM cache and matches byte for byte, also in CI.

Generality test, new domain
Polymer melt: unit conversion, hypothetical, new fact → v2, data-split advice, XRF partly outside the sources, contradicted premise, table, e-mail. Prompt injection and off-topic refused.
~590 backend and ~270 frontend tests run offline with fake models; CI on every push.

Limitations and next steps
What PRISM does not do yet, and the fix for each
Limitation today
Next step
Coverage: 71 curated cards; 129 drafted cards are unused until reviewed
→
AFS experts review the drafted cards; page-level retrieval over all AFS pages
Support strength: under half of judged claims are fully supported by their quote
→
Calibrate the judge on expert labels; the tooling is in place
Small gold set: 8 cases; 1 of 7 premise verdicts differs from the expert
→
Grow the gold set together with AFS experts
No measured spectra and no OCR of scanned pages
→
Attach measured spectra from the AFS lab to the feasibility plan
Prototype: no user accounts; enquiry text goes to the chosen LLM provider
→
Accounts and roles; an on-premise model for NDA enquiries
PRISM drafts the first assessment for an AFS expert to review; it does not replace that review.
